title: THE ADDED COST OF BUYING BACK

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'If the owner wishes to redeem the animal, a fifth must be added to its
value'" - Lev 27:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
If a person changed their mind and wanted to buy back what they had
dedicated, they could — but at an added cost. A fifth was added to the
value. Redeeming what had been given to God was possible, but it was
never treated as trivial.

That extra fifth is a small but meaningful detail. It ensured that people
would think carefully before making vows and before undoing them. Taking
back what was devoted to God was not to be done casually.

Dear reader, this teaches us to weigh our commitments before God with
seriousness. There is a cost to changing course on what we have set
apart for Him. Not because God is harsh, but because our word to Him
should mean something.

Yet there is a deeper thread here — the language of redemption, of buying
back at a price. Throughout Leviticus, redemption always costs something.
And that points us toward the greatest redemption of all.

We had been given over to sin, unable to buy ourselves back at any price.
And Christ redeemed us — not with an added fifth of silver, but with His
own blood (1 Pet 1:18-19). Paul says you were bought at a price;
therefore honour God with your body (1 Cor 6:20).

The cost of your redemption was infinite, and God paid it Himself. Live
today as someone who has been bought back at the greatest price.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I take my commitments to God seriously enough?
2. Have I grasped that my redemption cost Christ everything?
3. How should being "bought at a price" shape my choices today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, You redeemed me not with silver but with Your own blood. Help
me weigh my commitments to You honestly and to live as one who has been
bought back at such a cost. Amen.
